title: Effects of Neighbourhood Crime Prevention Measures on Citizens’ Perceptions of Crime: Blue-Light Patrols and Crime Maps
authors: 島田貴仁・雨宮護・菊池城治
authorsText: 島田貴仁・雨宮護・菊池城治
practiceOrganizations: National Research Institute of Police Science
practiceOrganizationsText: National Research Institute of Police Science
researchOrganizations: National Research Institute of Police Science
researchOrganizationsText: National Research Institute of Police Science
themesText: Community crime prevention / Fear of crime
intervention: Blue-light crime prevention patrols and public display of crime maps.
population: Residents of one city in the Tokyo metropolitan area.
comparison: Comparisons by awareness of the measures and related factors.
outcomes: Perceived victimisation risk, fear of crime, perceived neighbourhood safety, and residential satisfaction.
outcomesText: Perceived victimisation risk, fear of crime, perceived neighbourhood safety, and residential satisfaction.
result: Awareness of blue-light patrols was associated with higher perceived victimisation risk and lower neighbourhood satisfaction, while crime maps were associated with measures including neighbourhood satisfaction.
limitations: Observational study; the design does not directly estimate the causal effect of the interventions.
citation: Japanese Journal of Sociological Criminology 35, 132-148
notes: Retained because it evaluates public awareness and perception of crime prevention measures rather than intervention effects alone.

researchOrganizationsText: National Research Institute of Police Science
intervention: Crime prevention information combined with distribution of an additional bicycle lock.

comparison: Conditions differing in the information presented.
outcomes: Subsequent use of the distributed bicycle lock.
outcomesText: Subsequent use of the distributed bicycle lock.
result: The study measured subsequent lock use after participants received crime prevention information and an additional lock, to examine communication methods for encouraging preventive behaviour.
limitations: Described in the Police White Paper; details of allocation procedures and statistical results require confirmation from the original research report.
citation: Police White Paper 2011, Chapter 2, Section 5-6
notes: NRIPS field experiment. Original article or institute report remains a target for further tracing.

title: Changes in Young People’s Attitudes through Participation in a Shoplifting-Prevention Video Project (Part 2): Viewer Evaluation and Surveys of Participating University and Junior High School Students
authors: 大久保智生・時岡晴美・有馬道久・松浦隆夫・高橋護

intervention: Joint production and viewing of a shoplifting-prevention educational video.
population: University students, junior high school students, and video viewers.
comparison: Pre/post and related comparisons.
outcomes: Attitudes towards shoplifting and evaluation of the video.
outcomesText: Attitudes towards shoplifting and evaluation of the video.
sampleSize: Viewers 88; university students 17; junior high school students 31
result: Reported changes in attitudes towards shoplifting among participating university and junior high school students, together with favourable evaluations of the video.
limitations: Outcomes were mainly self-reported and did not directly measure changes in offending behaviour.
citation: Kagawa University Research in Educational Practice 25, 57-68
notes: Part of the long-running Kagawa Prefectural Police–Kagawa University collaboration.

title: Evidence-Based Practice in Shoplifting Prevention and Its Effects: Development, Use and Evaluation of a Store Shoplifting-Prevention Manual
authors: 時岡晴美・大久保智生・堀江良英・松永祐二
authorsText: 時岡晴美・大久保智生・堀江良英・松永祐二
intervention: Development and distribution of a retailer shoplifting-prevention manual based on research findings.
population: Retail stores in Kagawa Prefecture.
comparison: Use and implementation following distribution.
outcomes: Use of the manual, staff training, and evaluation of the initiative.
outcomesText: Use of the manual, staff training, and evaluation of the initiative.
result: Nearly half of stores reportedly used the manual for in-store placement or staff education, and around 90% evaluated the initiative positively.
limitations: Findings are based mainly on self-reported use and evaluation; causal effects on shoplifting reduction were not established.
citation: Kagawa University Faculty of Education Research Report, Part I 138, 75-81
notes: An early practice-oriented study in Japan explicitly framed around evidence-based crime prevention.

title: What Characteristics Distinguish Stores with High Levels of Shoplifting? Findings from a Survey of Retail Crime-Prevention Measures
authors: 大久保智生・堀江良英・松永祐二・永冨太一・時岡晴美
authorsText: 大久保智生・堀江良英・松永祐二・永冨太一・時岡晴美
intervention: Baseline assessment through a survey of retail stores.
population: Managers of 84 stores in Kagawa Prefecture.
comparison: Comparison of stores by shoplifting frequency.
outcomes: Store characteristics, responses, prevention measures, and managers’ attitudes.
outcomesText: Store characteristics, responses, prevention measures, and managers’ attitudes.
result: Associations between shoplifting frequency and store characteristics, responses, prevention measures and managerial attitudes were reported.
limitations: This was not a direct evaluation of an intervention.
citation: Kagawa University Faculty of Education Research Report, Part I 138, 11-21
notes: Retained as a baseline study informing subsequent manual and staff-engagement interventions.

title: Development and Implementation of an Educational Programme for Parents to Prevent Shoplifting among Young People

intervention: Educational programme for parents on preventing shoplifting among young people.
population: Parents.
comparison: Pre/post comparisons and related assessments.
outcomes: Knowledge and attitudes concerning shoplifting prevention.
outcomesText: Knowledge and attitudes concerning shoplifting prevention.
result: Developed and implemented a parent-focused education programme and examined its educational effects.
limitations: Crime incidence was not used as an outcome.
citation: Kagawa University Research in Educational Practice 26, 73-82
notes: Includes co-authorship by personnel from the prefectural police youth division.

title: An Evidence-Based Social Practice Cycle for Shoplifting Prevention: Development and Trial of an In-Store Staff Engagement Manual
authors: 大久保智生・岡田涼・時岡晴美・堀江良英・松下昌明・高橋護・尾崎祐士・藤沢隆行
authorsText: 大久保智生・岡田涼・時岡晴美・堀江良英・松下昌明・高橋護・尾崎祐士・藤沢隆行
intervention: Development of a manual for proactive staff engagement and trial implementation in retail stores.
population: Retail stores and store security personnel in Kagawa Prefecture.
comparison: Before/after and survey-informed comparisons.
outcomes: Staff engagement behaviour and store-side evaluations.
outcomesText: Staff engagement behaviour and store-side evaluations.
result: A manual was developed from store and security-staff surveys and trialled experimentally in stores, with an explicit cyclical model of evidence-based practice.
limitations: Details of effect estimation are limited, and any contribution to reductions in recorded shoplifting is not causally established.
citation: Kagawa University Faculty of Education Research Report, Part I 139, 35-51
notes: Explicitly presents a survey–development–implementation–evaluation cycle.

title: Evaluation of Shoplifting-Prevention Training and Educational Videos for Retail Stores
authors: 大久保智生・時岡晴美・岡田涼・尾崎祐士・藤沢隆行・有吉徳洋・西村雅之・松下昌明
authorsText: 大久保智生・時岡晴美・岡田涼・尾崎祐士・藤沢隆行・有吉徳洋・西村雅之・松下昌明
intervention: Training sessions for retail stores and a shoplifting-prevention video.
population: Retail personnel.
comparison: Training participants compared with video viewers.
outcomes: Overall evaluation and perceived usefulness of prevention measures.
outcomesText: Overall evaluation and perceived usefulness of prevention measures.
result: Training participants reported higher overall evaluations and a stronger sense of the usefulness of the measures than video viewers.
limitations: Self-reported outcomes; participants were not randomly assigned.
citation: Kagawa University Faculty of Education Research Report, Part I 142, 45-52
notes: Part of the Kagawa collaboration.

title: Effects of a Community Crime-Prevention Programme on Perceived Safety and Fear of Crime: The Chiba Convenience-Store Crime Prevention Box Model
authors: 山本功・島田貴仁
authorsText: 山本功・島田貴仁

practiceOrganizationsText: Chiba Prefectural Police and partners (model programme)
researchOrganizations: Shukutoku University / National Research Institute of Police Science
researchOrganizationsText: Shukutoku University / National Research Institute of Police Science
intervention: Convenience-store-based crime prevention box model programme.
population: Residents around two intervention locations.
comparison: Before versus after implementation.
outcomes: Perceived safety, perceived crime risk, and fear of crime.
outcomesText: Perceived safety, perceived crime risk, and fear of crime.
result: Perceived safety generally improved, while perceived risk and fear of crime increased in some measures or areas.
limitations: No randomisation; area-level and temporal differences may remain as confounders.
citation: Japanese Journal of Sociological Criminology 41, 80-97
notes: Important because the observed effects were not uniformly positive.

title: Crime Patterns and Crime-Prevention Measures at Convenience Stores: Evidence from the Fukuoka Prefectural Police Crime Prevention Research Adviser Programme
authors: 木下広章・柴田久・石橋知也・雨宮護・樋野公宏

researchOrganizationsText: Fukuoka University / University of Tsukuba / The University of Tokyo and collaborators
intervention: Policy development using crime-data analysis and field surveys of victimised and non-victimised stores.
population: 74 robbery-victimised stores and 74 nearby non-victimised stores.
comparison: Victimised versus non-victimised stores.
outcomes: Location and spatial environment, staff behaviour, and natural surveillance.
outcomesText: Location and spatial environment, staff behaviour, and natural surveillance.
design: Comparative observational study with field survey.
result: Findings highlighted staff behaviour, crime-prevention guidance, parking visibility and surveillance conditions created by shelving and store layout.
limitations: This was a policy-development study rather than a post-intervention effectiveness evaluation.
citation: City Planning Review / Papers on City Planning 51(3), 350-356
notes: Conducted within the Fukuoka Prefectural Police adviser programme.

title: Evaluation of Street CCTV in Entertainment Districts: Analysis under the Fukuoka Prefectural Police Crime Prevention Research Adviser Programme
authors: 雨宮護・樋野公宏・柴田久
authorsText: 雨宮護・樋野公宏・柴田久
researchOrganizations: University of Tsukuba / The University of Tokyo / Fukuoka University
researchOrganizationsText: University of Tsukuba / The University of Tokyo / Fukuoka University
intervention: Installation of street CCTV.
population: Hakata/Nakasu and Tenjin areas.
comparison: Before/after comparison with control areas.
outcomes: Violent offences, snatch theft, bicycle theft, vehicle-related crime, and spatial displacement.
outcomesText: Violent offences, snatch theft, bicycle theft, vehicle-related crime, and spatial displacement.
design: Quasi-experimental before/after evaluation with difference-in-differences and geographic analysis.
result: Relative reductions in theft-related offences were reported in Hakata/Nakasu, with no evidence of substantial crime displacement. Alignment between camera placement and pre-existing crime concentrations appeared important.
limitations: The number of areas was small and installation locations and local conditions differed.
citation: Urban Planning Reports 16(1), 18-23
notes: Conducted within the Fukuoka Prefectural Police adviser programme.

title: Spatio-Temporal Near-Repetition of Residential Burglary in Multi-Unit Housing: Analysis under the Fukuoka Prefectural Police Crime Prevention Research Adviser Programme
authors: 樋野公宏・雨宮護
authorsText: 樋野公宏・雨宮護
researchOrganizations: The University of Tokyo / University of Tsukuba
researchOrganizationsText: The University of Tokyo / University of Tsukuba
intervention: Use of police crime data to inform timely patrol and public-information measures.

comparison: Presence versus absence of spatio-temporal proximity.
outcomes: Repeat, near repeat and building-level near-repeat burglary patterns.
outcomesText: Repeat, near repeat and building-level near-repeat burglary patterns.
result: Near-repeat and same-building near-repeat patterns were identified, and interventions such as cocoon and neighbourhood watch approaches were proposed.
limitations: This was not a direct evaluation of an intervention.
citation: Urban Planning Reports 16(1), 24-27
notes: Retained as a foundation for subsequent intervention design.

population: Certified retail stores and related participants.
comparison: Comparison of certification and implementation status.
outcomes: Crime-prevention measures, collaboration and related attitudes.
outcomesText: Crime-prevention measures, collaboration and related attitudes.
result: Evaluated store-based crime prevention and community collaboration implemented through the certification scheme.

title: Evaluation of Training for Community Watch Volunteers and Crime-Prevention CSR Workshops for Retail Stores
authors: 大久保智生ほか
authorsText: 大久保智生ほか
intervention: Training for community watch volunteers and crime-prevention CSR workshops for stores.

comparison: Within-participant evaluation of training/workshop participation.
outcomes: Perceived meaning and key points of activity, and overall evaluation.
outcomesText: Perceived meaning and key points of activity, and overall evaluation.
result: Both groups reported favourable evaluations and a strong sense of the value of the activities, with positive associations between these measures.

title: Mismatch between Sexual-Offence Locations around a University and Female Students’ Perceptions of Risk: A Study in Jonan Ward, Fukuoka City
authors: 柴田久
authorsText: 柴田久
intervention: Combined police data, field observations and a survey of female university students to inform prevention behaviour.
population: Jonan Ward, Fukuoka City, and female university students.
comparison: Actual offence locations versus locations perceived as risky.
outcomes: Sexual-offence locations, perceived risk and crime-prevention awareness.
outcomesText: Sexual-offence locations, perceived risk and crime-prevention awareness.
design: Descriptive spatial analysis and perception survey.
sampleSize: 142 sexual offences; 28 priority cases and other data
result: A mismatch was identified between actual offence locations and places students perceived as risky, informing discussion of preventive behaviour and environmental improvements.
limitations: This was not a direct intervention evaluation.
citation: Fukuoka Prefectural Police Crime Prevention Research Adviser Programme, Research Findings Report No. 2
notes: Official Fukuoka Prefectural Police research report.

result: Multiple activities were implemented through a joint class with the prefectural police, including locking promotion and community safety mapping.

title: Effects of Visible Policing on Public Reassurance and Trust in the Police
authors: 島田貴仁・草尾祐樹

design: Process evaluation using an on-site survey.
result: Awareness was lower at commercial facilities, recognition accuracy varied by message, and some unlocked users reported an influence on locking intention.
limitations: Includes self-reported outcomes; should be interpreted alongside the behavioural-observation results in study (1).
citation: Journal of Environmental Psychology Research 14(1), 54
notes: Retained as a separate process-evaluation output from the same intervention.

title: Field Experiment Installing Anti-Voyeurism Mirrors at Railway Stations (1): Introduction through Crime-Prevention CSR and Evidence-Based Policy Making
authors: 井浩幸・久保江真・朝倉あずさ・後藤教利・島田貴仁
authorsText: 井浩幸・久保江真・朝倉あずさ・後藤教利・島田貴仁
intervention: Installation of anti-voyeurism mirrors on escalators at major stations, with observation of users’ head and gaze movements.
population: Major railway stations in Kyoto Prefecture.
comparison: Before versus after installation.
outcomes: Looking backwards or sideways while using escalators.
outcomesText: Looking backwards or sideways while using escalators.
sampleSize: Implemented at 18 locations in 10 stations; observed at 8 locations in 6 stations
result: One month after installation, looking behaviour was approximately four times the pre-intervention level. Findings were used to expand the measure to 41 locations at 28 stations.
limitations: Looking behaviour is an intermediate outcome; the causal effect on voyeurism incidents themselves was not established.
citation: Journal of Environmental Psychology Research 14(1), 35
notes: A useful EBPM example linking study findings to policy expansion.

title: Field Experiment Installing Anti-Voyeurism Mirrors at Railway Stations (2): Long-Term Follow-Up of the Persistence of Behaviour Change
authors: 久保江真・朝倉あずさ・後藤教利・井浩幸・島田貴仁
authorsText: 久保江真・朝倉あずさ・後藤教利・井浩幸・島田貴仁
intervention: Long-term follow-up of looking behaviour after installation of anti-voyeurism mirrors.
population: Escalator users at eight locations across six railway stations.
comparison: Pre-installation, 1 week, 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 months and 12 months.
outcomes: Looking backwards or sideways.
outcomesText: Looking backwards or sideways.
result: Intervention effects persisted overall over the longer term, with different patterns of attenuation by sex and age group.
limitations: Outcome was a behavioural indicator rather than recorded voyeurism; the user mix may differ across observation periods.
citation: Journal of Environmental Psychology Research 14(1), 60
notes: Long-term follow-up of study (1), examining persistence rather than short-term response alone.

title: Poster Experiment in Private Workplaces to Prevent Social-Media-Based Investment Fraud
authors: 萩谷遥平・大城海環・井上信輔・川内一郎・岩谷彩・木内聡・島田貴仁
authorsText: 萩谷遥平・大城海環・井上信輔・川内一郎・岩谷彩・木内聡・島田貴仁
researchOrganizations: Osaka University / Osaka Prefectural Police / Shiga University
researchOrganizationsText: Osaka University / Osaka Prefectural Police / Shiga University
intervention: Three anti-fraud posters displayed in employee break rooms at supermarkets in Osaka Prefecture.
population: Employees at 15 supermarkets.
comparison: Three poster conditions with pre/post assessment.
outcomes: Threat appraisal, behavioural task performance, and poster awareness/recognition.
outcomesText: Threat appraisal, behavioural task performance, and poster awareness/recognition.
design: Clustered field experiment with pre/post survey.
sampleSize: 615 pre and post; 234 awareness respondents; 156 in primary analysis
result: Poster awareness was about 38%. Even among those aware of the posters, effects on threat appraisal were limited, and most participants did nothing in response to a simulated advertisement.
limitations: Exposure to the intervention was low, creating a substantial implementation-fidelity problem. Analyses restricted to aware participants may be affected by selection bias.
citation: Journal of Environmental Psychology Research 14(1), 46
notes: Important null/implementation-failure case showing that disseminating information does not mean it was actually received.

title: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Factors Affecting Police Officers’ Continuation of an Initiative: An Award Scheme to Promote Applications for Suspension of International Telephone Service
authors: 金井大典・港淳平・島田貴仁
authorsText: 金井大典・港淳平・島田貴仁
themesText: Special fraud / Organisational behaviour / Recognition awards
intervention: Department-level awards for police officers promoting applications to suspend international telephone service.
population: Police officers eligible for awards within Nara Prefectural Police.
comparison: Officers who continued versus did not continue the initiative.
outcomes: Continuation, number of applications promoted, motivation and related measures.
outcomesText: Continuation, number of applications promoted, motivation and related measures.
design: Questionnaire and regression analysis following an organisational intervention.
result: Applications increased substantially after the award scheme was introduced. Continuing officers showed higher skills/habit and extrinsic motivation, although regression models did not show clear independent effects of the scale scores.
limitations: The causal effect of the award was not tested through randomisation; self-report and selection bias should be considered.
citation: Journal of Environmental Psychology Research 14(1), 47
notes: Unusual example focusing on sustained implementation inside a police organisation rather than resident-facing intervention.

title: Evaluating voice-message-based shoplifting prevention using a human-shaped device: evidence from a field experiment in supermarket stores in Japan
authors: Ai Suzuki
authorsText: Ai Suzuki
intervention: Six voice-message conditions delivered through a police-officer-shaped device in retail product areas.
population: 13 intervention stores and 3 control stores.
comparison: Intervention versus control stores, same-month previous-year comparison, and message-condition comparisons.
outcomes: Loss rate for seven target product categories.
outcomesText: Loss rate for seven target product categories.
result: Effects varied by product. Messages appealing to moral norms or conscience were the most effective under some conditions.
limitations: The intervention did not work uniformly across all products; comparisons include previous-year periods, so store and temporal factors require caution.
citation: Journal of Experimental Criminology
notes: Peer-reviewed publication of the previously recorded Fukushima Prefectural Police field experiment.

title: Plural policing in rural contexts: a GPS-based evaluation of multi-entity patrols against fruit theft
authors: Mamoru Amemiya・Ai Suzuki・Takahito Shimada・Hideharu Kurita
authorsText: Mamoru Amemiya・Ai Suzuki・Takahito Shimada・Hideharu Kurita
practiceOrganizations: Yamanashi Prefectural Police and other local actors
practiceOrganizationsText: Yamanashi Prefectural Police and other local actors
intervention: GPS tracking of fruit-theft prevention patrols conducted by police, local government, agricultural cooperatives, NPOs and other actors.
population: Patrols by six organisations across two municipalities in Yamanashi Prefecture.
comparison: Comparison of patrol characteristics across organisations.
outcomes: Temporal and spatial coverage and movement characteristics.
outcomesText: Temporal and spatial coverage and movement characteristics.
design: Implementation and coverage evaluation using GPS behavioural data.
result: Different organisations showed complementary patrol patterns, quantitatively expanding temporal and spatial coverage.
limitations: The study evaluated patrol implementation and deployment rather than estimating reductions in recorded crime.
citation: Security Journal 39, Article 28
notes: Japanese case quantitatively evaluating plural policing in a rural setting.

title: Promoting Caller-Verification Behaviour among Older Adults to Prevent Special Fraud: Social-Norm and Behaviour-Change Approaches
authors: 島田貴仁・齊藤知範・山根由子・倉石宏樹・春田悠佳・大竹文雄
authorsText: 島田貴仁・齊藤知範・山根由子・倉石宏樹・春田悠佳・大竹文雄
practiceOrganizations: Shiga Prefectural Police / two police stations in Shiga Prefecture / National Research Institute of Police Science
practiceOrganizationsText: Shiga Prefectural Police / two police stations in Shiga Prefecture / National Research Institute of Police Science
researchOrganizations: National Research Institute of Police Science / Shiga Prefectural Police / Sophia University graduate school / Osaka University
researchOrganizationsText: National Research Institute of Police Science / Shiga Prefectural Police / Sophia University graduate school / Osaka University
themesText: Special fraud / Landline telephones / Social norms and behavioural rehearsal
intervention: Five intervention conditions including threat messaging, altruistic messaging, instructions for voicemail use, in-person rehearsal with a simulated telephone, and a follow-up confirmation call after returning home.
population: Older adults with a home landline who visited two police stations in Shiga Prefecture for licence renewal or related services.
comparison: Assignment to one of five intervention conditions by day.
outcomes: Whether the participant used voicemail to verify the caller during an actual telephone response one week after intervention.
outcomesText: Whether the participant used voicemail to verify the caller during an actual telephone response one week after intervention.
design: Field experiment with condition assignment and behavioural observation.
sampleSize: 597 participants; 284 who answered a call one week later were analysed
result: The altruistic-message condition and the in-person rehearsal condition increased caller-verification behaviour by about 20 percentage points relative to control or comparison conditions. A home-practice condition showed no improvement.
limitations: Outcome was measured at a single point one week after intervention. Behaviour change occurred in at most about half of participants, and assignment was by intervention day rather than fully individual randomisation.
citation: 16th Annual Conference of the Association of Behavioral Economics and Finance, 2C03
notes: Consistent with Fumio Ohtake’s KAKENHI project 20H05632; a clear researcher–practitioner collaboration in which police personnel delivered the intervention and behavioural measurement.

title: Preventing Voyeurism by Installing Mirrors on Railway-Station Escalators: A Field Experiment of Environmental-Cue Nudges
authors: 島田貴仁・大沼貴志・齊藤知範・大竹文雄
authorsText: 島田貴仁・大沼貴志・齊藤知範・大竹文雄
practiceOrganizations: National Research Institute of Police Science
practiceOrganizationsText: National Research Institute of Police Science
researchOrganizations: National Research Institute of Police Science / Osaka University
researchOrganizationsText: National Research Institute of Police Science / Osaka University
intervention: Installation of large mirrors, small mirrors and posters in combinations on upward escalators to encourage users to look behind them.
population: Escalator users at 16 locations across four stations in Saitama Prefecture.
comparison: Poster present/absent × large/small/no mirror conditions, with before/after comparison.
outcomes: Whether users looked behind them.
outcomesText: Whether users looked behind them.
design: Field experiment with condition assignment and pre/post behavioural observation.
result: After mirrors and posters were installed, up to around 20% of users looked behind them. In multivariable regression, mirror installation alone significantly increased looking behaviour.
limitations: The outcome was looking behaviour assumed to reduce opportunities for voyeurism rather than recorded crime incidence. Station and facility conditions may confound estimates.
citation: 18th Annual Conference of the Association of Behavioral Economics and Finance, K03_PR0067
notes: Important precursor to the later Kyoto Prefectural Police anti-voyeurism mirror implementation and long-term follow-up.

title: Effects of Newspaper Crime-Prevention Information on Attitudes towards Special Fraud
authors: 讃井知・島田貴仁・荒井崇史
authorsText: 讃井知・島田貴仁・荒井崇史
practiceOrganizations: National Research Institute of Police Science (co-author affiliation)
practiceOrganizationsText: National Research Institute of Police Science (co-author affiliation)
researchOrganizations: University of Tsukuba / National Research Institute of Police Science / Tohoku University
researchOrganizationsText: University of Tsukuba / National Research Institute of Police Science / Tohoku University
intervention: Exposure to a special-fraud feature article in a local newspaper in Yamagata Prefecture.
population: Internet panel participants aged 20–69.
comparison: Exposure versus non-exposure to the newspaper article across three waves.
outcomes: Attitudes towards special fraud, general and specific preventive behavioural intentions, and behaviour change.
outcomesText: Attitudes towards special fraud, general and specific preventive behavioural intentions, and behaviour change.
design: Three-wave longitudinal survey evaluating natural exposure.
result: Exposure to the newspaper article increased general intentions to prevent victimisation, but no statistically significant effect was found for more specific preventive intentions or actual behaviour change.
limitations: Exposure was not randomly assigned and was subject to self-selection; actual reductions in fraud victimisation were not directly measured.
citation: 85th Annual Convention of the Japanese Psychological Association, PC-116
notes: Part of Tomo Sanui’s crime-prevention information research stream; another example of the gap between information exposure, intention and concrete behaviour.

title: Analysis of Bicycle-Theft Victimisation Risk in Public Bicycle-Parking Facilities
authors: 大沼貴志・齊藤知範・島田貴仁
authorsText: 大沼貴志・齊藤知範・島田貴仁
practiceOrganizations: National Research Institute of Police Science
practiceOrganizationsText: National Research Institute of Police Science
researchOrganizations: National Research Institute of Police Science
researchOrganizationsText: National Research Institute of Police Science
intervention: Spatial analysis of environmental attributes of public bicycle-parking facilities and bicycle-theft victimisation risk.
population: Public bicycle-parking facilities in Saitama Prefecture (details require confirmation from the original paper; the later abstract reports 417 facilities).
comparison: Comparison across environmental attributes of bicycle-parking facilities and railway stations.
outcomes: Bicycle-theft victimisation risk.
outcomesText: Bicycle-theft victimisation risk.
design: Observational study / GIS analysis (detailed methods require confirmation from the original paper).
sampleSize: Requires confirmation from the original paper (the later abstract reports 417 facilities and 5,172 theft incidents).
result: Reported a bicycle-theft victimisation-risk analysis of public bicycle-parking facilities in Saitama Prefecture at the GIS Association of Japan conference. Detailed findings require confirmation from the original paper.
limitations: Bibliographic details have been confirmed through J-GLOBAL. Methods and statistical findings are not assumed to be identical to the later 2025 conference abstract and remain pending confirmation from the original paper.
citation: GIS Association of Japan Conference Proceedings 2024, P2-31
notes: A separate publication within the same research stream as the 2025 environmental-psychology and behaviormetrics conference abstracts.

title: Victimisation Risk Analysis of Bicycle Theft: Environmental Factors at Public Bicycle-Parking Facilities and Railway Stations
authors: 大沼貴志・齊藤知範・島田貴仁
authorsText: 大沼貴志・齊藤知範・島田貴仁
practiceOrganizations: Saitama Prefectural Police / National Research Institute of Police Science
practiceOrganizationsText: Saitama Prefectural Police / National Research Institute of Police Science
researchOrganizations: Saitama Prefectural Police / National Research Institute of Police Science / Shiga University
researchOrganizationsText: Saitama Prefectural Police / National Research Institute of Police Science / Shiga University
themesText: Bicycle theft / Environmental criminology / Police data analysis
intervention: Analysis of structural and facility characteristics of 417 public bicycle-parking facilities and bicycle-theft victimisation over 66 months.
population: 417 public bicycle-parking facilities around railway stations in 63 municipalities in Saitama Prefecture.
comparison: Comparison across environmental attributes of bicycle-parking facilities and railway stations, including propensity-score matching.
outcomes: 5,172 bicycle-theft victimisation incidents over 66 months.
outcomesText: 5,172 bicycle-theft victimisation incidents over 66 months.
design: Multilevel negative-binomial regression and propensity-score matching.
result: Risk was lower at less conspicuous locations and at facilities with attendants, and higher at on-street and free bicycle-parking facilities. After accounting for the station-level share of thefts, some factors were no longer statistically significant; in matched analyses, CCTV and free parking remained significant while attendants did not.
limitations: Observational study; causal effects are not established. Some estimates change depending on how station-level victimisation share is handled, and facility selection and unobserved confounding remain relevant.
citation: Proceedings of the 53rd Annual Meeting of the Behaviormetric Society of Japan, 262-263
notes: A separate publication within the same research stream as the 2025 environmental-psychology abstract. A Saitama Prefectural Police affiliation is explicitly recorded in the master.
